  (the address pinned at schedule time goes stale on session switch/restart
  and would strand the reminder) — EXCEPT self-addressed records naming a
  subagent mailbox of this session (`<prefix>/<childId>`, gh-970): those
  deliver as recorded (the address rides the same owner prefix and is as
  stable; re-addressing stole the child's reminder into main), and the
  tool's `senderMailbox` override (host-wired from `activeSubagentId()`)

  main's — hosts re-arm on every mailbox change
  (CLI `_syncMailboxPrefix`, app `_setMailboxPrefix`) and sweep due records
  on their inbox ticks; `dispose()` cancels only the timer, the files stay.
  gh-1180: a re-addressed SELF record also delivers FROM the live mailbox
  (`from` rewritten alongside `to` in `_deliverDueInner`) — an adopted
  reminder keeps the self shape (from == to) the wake policy needs to
  classify it exempt, so a chain survives a session-id change. Every
  lifecycle step lands in the receipt trail
  (`<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl`, `ScheduledReceiptLog`,
  best-effort): scheduled / delivered / delivery_failed / scan_failed
  (queue) and wake_attempted / turn_started / wake_refused (both hosts'
  wake paths; refusal receipts are once per refusal EPISODE — the latch
  lives in `InboxWakePolicy` next to the streak, so a held gate cannot
  spam the trail and a repeat episode after user input is receipted
  again).
  Sleep resilience (issue #259): all due math rides an injectable wall
  clock (`ScheduledMessageQueue(clock:)`), long waits are split into ≤60s
  timer legs (`maxTimerLeg`) that recompute the remaining delay from the
  wall clock on every fire — never accumulating duration drift — and
  hosts run a catch-up sweep at every TURN START (CLI `_beginUserPrompt`,
  app `sendText`) in addition to the idle inbox ticks, so the first
  post-sleep turn delivers every overdue record immediately. Catch-up is
  exactly-once per record (file removed on send + the `_delivering`
  in-flight guard) — missed cycles of a recurring self-re-arm are NOT
  replayed; the re-armed cycle simply resumes from "now". For true
  sleep-proofing (delivery DURING lid sleep) no in-process timer can
  help: add an external pinger, e.g. a cron/launchd entry that messages
  the session's mailbox — mail to an asleep session already launches a
  headless wake run that drains the inbox and sweeps due records.
 Failure isolation (issue #270): a throwing `send` is contained per
 record (logged via `onError` — CLI `[sched]` line, app `AppLog`), the
 record stays for the next sweep, and the post-failure re-arm floors the
 leg at `failureBackoff` (60s) so a poison record cannot spin a
 zero-delay timer; sweeps deliver in due-time order, and the app's
 turn-start sweep is awaited so the fresh turn sees the fired reminder.
 A failed SCAN (transient `listDir`/read error on a leg, gh-1180) is
 equally loud: `onError` + a `scan_failed` receipt, then a re-arm at
 `failureBackoff` — the arming heartbeat never silently disarms
 ("scan failed" used to be treated as "nothing pending", permanently
 disarming the scheduler with zero log). Corrupt record CONTENT is
 still skipped, not fatal (issue #59). Every lifecycle step is
 receipted to an append-only JSONL trail at
 `<messagesRoot>/_scheduled/receipts.jsonl` (`ScheduledReceiptLog`,
 gh-1180): `scheduled` / `delivered` (with lag) / `delivery_failed` /
 `scan_failed` from the queue, plus host-side `wake_attempted` /
 `turn_started` / `wake_refused` (with reason) from the CLI wake path —
 a post-mortem can distinguish "timer never fired" (no `delivered`)
 from "wake refused" without reading source. The trail is best-effort:
 a failing write logs via `onError` and never breaks scheduling.
 Records carry the scheduling instance's `owner` (mailbox prefix): a
 sweeper re-addresses a self-addressed record only when the stored owner
 matches its own prefix, and never deletes another instance's record -
 foreign-owned records are left where their owner sweeps (also across a
 root change: only own records migrate to an adopted folder's root).
 Legacy untagged records drain via the old any-sweeper path; records
 whose owner session is deleted (`/reset` mints a new id) stay on disk -
 there is no reaper, cleanup is manual. `agent_fabric` resolves the
 messages root lazily per sweep (was: pinned to the launch cwd at
 construction), and pending records migrate across a root change, so a
 session-folder adoption carries the reminders along instead of
 stranding them under the launch cwd.


  The `## Agent messaging` prompt section (prompts messaging_section.md, CLI +
  app variants) tells the model its own mailbox address. Turn-boundary
  delivery: `Agent.externalSteeringSource`
  merges inbox drains into the steering poll (main in AgentCli/AgentService
  as `_mainInboxMessages`, children via the executor) — messages land as
  sender-attributed user messages, so they persist in the session and read
  like a chat. Idle wake: an inbox watcher (2s CLI / 3s app) starts a turn
  when mail arrives while idle — two Fa instances chat live; a 10-run
  streak cap without user input breaks agent-to-agent ping-pong loops.
  The lanes live in `InboxWakePolicy` (gh-1180): user-kind mail always
  wakes and resets the streak (gating it would deadlock:
  no run → no reset → no run); a delivered `schedule_message`
  self-reminder (`[scheduled] ` prefix, from == to) is EXEMPT from the
  cap — a deliberate agent-chosen cadence (night watch, periodic sweep)
  wakes forever, with a 30s cadence floor so a zero-delay re-schedule
  spin is still bounded like chatter; foreign agent chatter stays
  capped. A refused wake is never silent: one dim `[mail] wake refused`
  line per episode and a `wake_refused` receipt.
  UI: `/agents` rows show a `mail:N` pending marker (the CLI
  font has no ✉ glyph), the app's AgentsSection shows `✉N`; observe/detail
  views list the pending inbox.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ProgramBench results ledger upsert (gh-182).

`bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's
OWN ProgramBench results — per-instance score/tests, cost, calls,
provider/model, run id + artifact links, and the smoke|lite|full mode —
the `fa_results.json` pattern applied to bench-programbench.yml. It is
written by the bench-programbench.yml aggregate step on every GREEN run
(summary verdict + Tier-0 `submit verify` passed) and by hand for
backfills (the seed smoke row was recorded this way).

Usage:

    pbench_record.py --stats-dir pbench-run/<RUN_ID>/_stats \
        --taskset-ref 895f65916bc5 --pbench-version 1.2.5 \
        --model kimi-for-coding --mode smoke --total 201 \
        [--fa-version 2fd100169e] [--date 2026-10-24] \
        [--run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/40072410719]... \
        [--artifact "programbench-submission=<url>"]...

`--stats-dir` is the merged run dir's `_stats/` written by `programbench
submit package` + summary.py: score.json (the per-instance
{branch/test: bool} map), cost.json + calls.json (self-reported, from
the fa session logs). Score pct = share of that instance's scored tests
that passed; solved = every scored test true (summary.py's ✅
convention).

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (taskset_ref, model, mode) —
one row per task-set pin x model x mode. Re-recording the same job
updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls / artifact_urls
(same label -> URL updated); it never appends a duplicate row. A mode
change (smoke -> full) is a NEW row: the smoke proof (attempted << the
official total) must survive next to the headline run, never be
overwritten by it. Renders (pbench_render.py) sort full runs first and
label smoke rows as pipeline proofs — a smoke result is never presented
as a leaderboard headline.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool. Nothing here writes the official ProgramBench registry —
submission stays a manual self-serve PR decision by the owner
(docs/bench.md).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("pbench_results.json")

# The closed dispatch-mode set — tasks.py's `_select` outputs (the
# workflow's setup `mode` output). Unknown modes fail here instead of
# rendering as an unlabeled row.
MODES = ("smoke", "lite", "globs", "full")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str, str]":
    return (row.get("taskset_ref", ""), row.get("model", ""),
            row.get("mode", ""))


def read_stats(stats_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """Per-instance entries from the packaged `_stats/` maps.

    score.json is the required input (a green aggregate always has it —
    the verdict gate fails the run before record is reached otherwise);
    cost.json/calls.json entries ride along when present. An instance
    known only from cost/calls still lands with no score fields — a gap
    must render as "no score", never silently disappear.
    """
    score_path = stats_dir / "score.json"
    score = json.loads(score_path.read_text()) if score_path.is_file() else None
    if score is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no score.json under {stats_dir} — "
                                "record runs only after `programbench "
                                "submit package`")
    costs = json.loads((stats_dir / "cost.json").read_text()) \
        if (stats_dir / "cost.json").is_file() else {}
    calls = json.loads((stats_dir / "calls.json").read_text()) \
        if (stats_dir / "calls.json").is_file() else {}

    instances: dict = {}
    for iid in sorted(set(score) | set(costs) | set(calls)):
        entry: dict = {}
        tests = score.get(iid)
        if isinstance(tests, dict) and tests:
            passed = sum(1 for v in tests.values() if v is True)
            entry["score_pct"] = round(100.0 * passed / len(tests), 1)
            entry["tests"] = len(tests)
            entry["solved"] = passed == len(tests)
        if iid in costs:
            entry["cost_usd"] = round(float(costs[iid]), 4)
        if iid in calls:
            entry["calls"] = int(calls[iid])
        instances[iid] = entry
    return instances


def upsert(doc: dict, *, taskset_ref: str, model: str, mode: str, total: int,
           instances: dict = None, date: str = None,
           pbench_version: str = None, fa_version: str = None,
           run_urls: "list[str]" = (),
           artifacts: "list[dict]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (taskset_ref, model, mode) row.

    Existing run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) and artifact_urls
    merged by label so a job re-run updates instead of duplicating;
    numbers/date reflect the latest record call. `instances=None`
    keeps the row's existing per-instance data (a URL-only touch-up).
    """
    if mode not in MODES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown mode {mode!r} — expected one of "
                         f"{', '.join(MODES)} (tasks.py's output set)")
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (taskset_ref, model, mode):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"taskset_ref": taskset_ref, "model": model, "mode": mode}
        doc["results"].append(row)
    if instances is None:
        instances = row.get("instances") or {}

    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    by_label = {a["label"]: a["url"] for a in row.get("artifact_urls") or []}
    for a in artifacts or ():
        if a.get("label") and a.get("url"):
            by_label[a["label"]] = a["url"]

    scores = [e["score_pct"] for e in instances.values()
              if isinstance(e.get("score_pct"), (int, float))]
    costs = [e["cost_usd"] for e in instances.values()
             if isinstance(e.get("cost_usd"), (int, float))]
    calls = [e["calls"] for e in instances.values()
             if isinstance(e.get("calls"), int)]

    row.update(
        {
            "date": date or datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat(),
            "total": int(total),
            "attempted": len(instances),
            "solved": sum(1 for e in instances.values()
                          if e.get("solved") is True),
            "instances": dict(sorted(instances.items())),
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            "artifact_urls": [{"label": k, "url": by_label[k]}
                              for k in sorted(by_label)],
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-182 R4).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    row["score_pct"] = round(sum(scores) / len(scores), 1) if scores else None
    row["cost_usd"] = round(sum(costs), 4) if costs else None
    row["calls"] = sum(calls) if calls else None
    if pbench_version:
        row["pbench_version"] = pbench_version
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: task-set pin, then model, then mode — deterministic
    # for merges; the renderer applies its own presentation order.
    doc["results"].sort(key=_key)
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--stats-dir", type=Path, required=True,
                        help="merged run dir's _stats/ (score/cost/calls)")
    parser.add_argument("--taskset-ref", dest="taskset_ref", required=True,
                        help="facebookresearch/ProgramBench pin (short sha)")
    parser.add_argument("--pbench-version", dest="pbench_version",
                        help="PyPI programbench pin the run evaluated with")
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True,
                        help="provider model id (the resolved bench_model)")
    parser.add_argument("--mode", required=True,
                        help="dispatch mode from tasks.py (smoke/lite/"
                             "globs/full)")
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int, required=True,
                        help="FULL official instance count (the dilution "
                             "denominator; tasks.py's `total` output)")
    parser.add_argument("--date",
                        help="run date YYYY-MM-DD (default: today UTC)")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version",
                        help="fa ref the run executed")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])
    parser.add_argument("--artifact", dest="artifacts", action="append",
                        default=[], metavar="LABEL=URL",
                        help="analysis-artifact link (repeatable)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.mode not in MODES:
        print(f"error: --mode must be one of {', '.join(MODES)} — "
              f"got: {args.mode!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    artifacts = []
    for spec in args.artifacts:
        label, sep, url = spec.partition("=")
        if not sep or not label.strip() or not url.strip():
            print("error: --artifact must be LABEL=URL — got: "
                  f"{spec!r}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        artifacts.append({"label": label.strip(), "url": url.strip()})
    if args.total < 0:
        print("error: --total must be >= 0", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    try:
        instances = read_stats(args.stats_dir)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"error: --stats-dir {args.stats_dir}: {exc}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    doc = load_ledger(args.ledger)
    row = upsert(doc, taskset_ref=args.taskset_ref, model=args.model,
                 mode=args.mode, total=args.total, instances=instances,
                 date=args.date, pbench_version=args.pbench_version,
                 fa_version=args.fa_version, run_urls=args.run_urls,
                 artifacts=artifacts)
    save_ledger(doc, args.ledger)
    print(json.dumps(row, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Unit tests for the gh-182 ProgramBench leaderboard tooling.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/leaderboard

Hermetic: the record tests build synthetic _stats dirs in a temp dir and
the render tests feed ledger dicts directly — no test touches the
network (the run/artifact URLs are plain strings by contract).
"""
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import pbench_record
import pbench_render


def _write_stats(stats_dir: Path, score: dict, costs: dict = None,
                 calls: dict = None) -> Path:
    stats_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (stats_dir / "score.json").write_text(json.dumps(score))
    (stats_dir / "cost.json").write_text(json.dumps(costs or {}))
    (stats_dir / "calls.json").write_text(json.dumps(calls or {}))
    return stats_dir


def _ledger_row(**kw) -> dict:
    """A minimal full-run row for render tests."""
    fields = dict(
        taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
        model="kimi-for-coding", mode="full", total=201,
        date="2026-11-02", fa_version="abc123456789",
        run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/500"],
        artifacts=[{"label": "programbench-submission",
                    "url": "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/500/artifacts/42"}],
        instances={
            "cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0, "tests": 506, "solved": True,
                        "cost_usd": 0.42, "calls": 57},
        },
    )
    fields.update(kw)
    doc = {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    pbench_record.upsert(doc, **fields)
    return doc


class PbenchRecordTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.ledger = Path(self.tmp.name) / "pbench_results.json"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def _record(self, **kw):
        doc = pbench_record.load_ledger(self.ledger)
        row = pbench_record.upsert(doc, **kw)
        pbench_record.save_ledger(doc, self.ledger)
        return json.loads(self.ledger.read_text())

    def test_seed_row_is_self_reported(self):
        doc = self._record(
            taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
            date="2026-10-24",
            instances={"cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0, "tests": 506,
                                   "solved": True}})
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertTrue(row["self_reported"])
        self.assertEqual(row["mode"], "smoke")
        self.assertEqual(row["attempted"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row["solved"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(row["score_pct"], 98.0)
        self.assertEqual(row["taskset_ref"], "895f65916bc5")

    def test_rerun_same_job_updates_not_duplicates(self):
        url = "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719"
        self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                     model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
                     date="2026-10-24", run_urls=[url],
                     instances={"cmatrix": {"score_pct": 90.0, "tests": 10,
                                            "solved": False}})
        doc = self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                           model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
                           date="2026-10-25", run_urls=[url],
                           instances={"cmatrix": {"score_pct": 98.0,
                                                  "tests": 506,
                                                  "solved": True}})
        self.assertEqual(len(doc["results"]), 1)
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["run_urls"], [url])  # deduped, not doubled
        self.assertEqual(row["date"], "2026-10-25")
        self.assertEqual(row["instances"]["cmatrix"]["score_pct"], 98.0)

    def test_mode_change_is_a_new_row(self):
        # A later full run must NOT overwrite the smoke proof row — the
        # smoke row stays recorded as the pipeline proof it was.
        self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                     model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
                     date="2026-10-24", instances={})
        doc = self._record(taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
                           model="kimi-for-coding", mode="full", total=201,
                           date="2026-11-02", instances={})
        self.assertEqual(len(doc["results"]), 2)
        self.assertEqual({r["mode"] for r in doc["results"]},
                         {"smoke", "full"})

    def test_multi_run_and_artifact_union(self):
        doc = self._record(
            taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
            date="2026-10-24",
            run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/1"],
            artifacts=[{"label": "programbench-submission",
                        "url": "https://github.com/o/r/a/1"}])
        doc = self._record(
            taskset_ref="895f65916bc5", pbench_version="1.2.5",
            model="kimi-for-coding", mode="smoke", total=201,
            date="2026-10-25",
            run_urls=["https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/1",
                      "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/2"],
            artifacts=[{"label": "programbench-submission",
                        "url": "https://github.com/o/r/a/2"}])
        row = doc["results"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["run_urls"], [
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/1",
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/2"])
        # Same label -> URL updated in place, never duplicated.
        self.assertEqual(row["artifact_urls"], [
            {"label": "programbench-submission",
             "url": "https://github.com/o/r/a/2"}])

    def test_read_stats_parses_score_cost_calls(self):
        stats = _write_stats(
            Path(self.tmp.name) / "_stats",
            score={"cmatrix": {"t/a": True, "t/b": True, "t/c": False},
                   "zip-password-finder": {"t/a": True}},
            costs={"cmatrix": 0.41678, "zip-password-finder": 0.5},
            calls={"cmatrix": 57, "zip-password-finder": 61})
        instances = pbench_record.read_stats(stats)
        self.assertEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["score_pct"], 66.7)
        self.assertEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["tests"], 3)
        self.assertFalse(instances["cmatrix"]["solved"])
        self.assertAlmostEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["cost_usd"], 0.4168)
        self.assertEqual(instances["cmatrix"]["calls"], 57)
        self.assertTrue(instances["zip-password-finder"]["solved"])
        # An instance with calls but no score map still lands (honest
        # gap: rendered as "no score"), never silently dropped.
        self.assertIn("zip-password-finder", instances)

    def test_read_stats_missing_score_json_errors(self):
        with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
            pbench_record.read_stats(Path(self.tmp.name) / "nope")

    def test_main_writes_ledger_from_stats_dir(self):
        stats = _write_stats(
            Path(self.tmp.name) / "_stats",
            score={"cmatrix": {"t/a": True, "t/b": True}},
            costs={"cmatrix": 0.25}, calls={"cmatrix": 9})
        rc = pbench_record.main([
            "--ledger", str(self.ledger), "--stats-dir", str(stats),
            "--mode", "smoke", "--model", "kimi-for-coding",
            "--pbench-version", "1.2.5", "--taskset-ref", "895f65916bc5",
            "--total", "201", "--fa-version", "abc123456789",
            "--date", "2026-10-24",
            "--run-url", "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/7",
            "--artifact",

        self.assertIn("2 of 201", section)
        self.assertIn("⭐ kimi-for-coding", section)
        self.assertIn("self-reported", section.lower())

        self.assertIn("never auto-submitted", section)

        doc = self._smoke_ledger()
        pbench_record.upsert(

            model="glm-5.3-flash", mode="full", total=201,

        self.assertIn("| cmatrix | 98.0% | 506 | ✅ | $0.42 | 57 |", section)

    def test_missing_artifacts_fall_back_to_run_link(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        self.assertIn("see the [run page]", section.lower())
        self.assertIn(
            "https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719", section)

    def test_splice_roundtrip_and_idempotency(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        text = ("<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->\n\n"
                "## What's inside\n\nbody\n")
        once = pbench_render.splice_readme(text, section)
        self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN, once)
        self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_END, once)
        # Inserted after the Terminal-Bench region, before the anchor
        # heading, which survives.
        self.assertLess(once.index("<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->"),
                        once.index(pbench_render.SECTION_HEADER))
        self.assertLess(once.index(pbench_render.SECTION_HEADER),
                        once.index("## What's inside"))
        # A second splice replaces — no duplicated blocks.
        twice = pbench_render.splice_readme(once, section)
        self.assertEqual(once.count(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN), 1)
        self.assertEqual(twice, once)

    def test_splice_without_anchor_inserts_before_heading(self):
        section = pbench_render.render_section(self._smoke_ledger())
        out = pbench_render.splice_readme("# Only a title\n", section)
        self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN, out)

    def test_html_page_renders_same_block(self):
        html = pbench_render.render_html(self._smoke_ledger())
        self.assertIn("<!doctype html>", html.lower())
        self.assertIn("ProgramBench", html)
        self.assertIn("pipeline proof", html)
        self.assertIn("2 of 201", html)
        self.assertIn("⭐ kimi-for-coding", html)
        self.assertIn("https://github.com/o/r/actions/runs/40072410719", html)
        # Instance ids are machine data — never interpolated raw.
        self.assertNotIn("<cmatrix>", html)

    def test_html_escapes_instance_ids(self):
        doc = _ledger_row(instances={
            "<script>alert(1)</script>": {"score_pct": 50.0, "tests": 2,
                                          "solved": False},
        })
        html = pbench_render.render_html(doc)
        self.assertNotIn("<script>alert(1)</script>", html)
        self.assertIn("<script>", html)

    def test_main_writes_readme_and_html_and_check(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            readme = Path(tmp) / "README.md"
            readme.write_text(
                "<!-- leaderboard:end (gh-1682) -->\n\n"
                "## What's inside\n\nbody\n")
            html = Path(tmp) / "programbench.html"
            ledger = Path(tmp) / "pbench_results.json"
            ledger.write_text(json.dumps(self._smoke_ledger()))
            argv = ["--readme", str(readme), "--ledger", str(ledger),
                    "--html", str(html)]
            self.assertEqual(pbench_render.main(argv + ["--check"]), 1)
            self.assertEqual(pbench_render.main(argv), 0)
            self.assertIn(pbench_render.MARKER_BEGIN, readme.read_text())
            self.assertIn("pipeline proof", html.read_text())
            # Second run is a no-op (idempotent), --check agrees.
            self.assertEqual(pbench_render.main(argv + ["--check"]), 0)

    def test_main_requires_a_surface(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            ledger = Path(tmp) / "pbench_results.json"
            ledger.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": 1, "results": []}))
            self.assertEqual(
                pbench_render.main(["--ledger", str(ledger)]), 2)

      # package step derives submission_id from the dir name). The

      # tree is already the full run dir; attempt-1 leftovers (gh-1658
      # RCA copies) are excluded from the fold.

          set -euo pipefail

            cp -R "$d"/. "$RUN_DIR/"

name: Bench ProgramBench

# Runs the fa coding agent against ProgramBench
# (facebookresearch/ProgramBench — "rebuild a complete codebase from a
# compiled binary + its docs") and produces a SUBMISSION-READY artifact
# set for the self-serve leaderboard (issue #1685): the aggregate job runs
# `programbench submit package` and `programbench submit verify` (Tier-0)
# over the merged run dir, so the uploaded artifact is exactly the folder
# a maintainer PRs to ProgramBench/submissions (pointer.yaml +
# submission.yaml + _stats/, per the registry README).
#
# Shape: same as bench-harbor.yml (gh-1124 family) — build the fa bundle
# once in setup, shard the task set into a matrix, solve+eval per shard,
# aggregate + verdict last. Tasks run in docker on GH hosted runners
# (x86_64 images — the usage guide warns they will not run on arm hosts).
#
# Internet rule, enforced not honored: ProgramBench bans agent internet
# access at inference (fetching the original source is disqualification).
# fa's LLM calls originate INSIDE the task container (the harbor-proven
# pattern, bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py), so each task container is moved
# onto a docker `--internal` network (no external route) and gets exactly
# ONE egress route: the selected provider's API endpoint, via a host-side
# L4 forwarder (bench/programbench/llm_forwarder.py) bound to the network
# gateway. TLS is end-to-end (SNI + cert stay the provider's real ones —
# fa's baseUrl is byte-identical to a direct run). The agent cannot reach
# anything else. CA roots + the fa bundle are installed BEFORE the
# container leaves the internet-facing boot network (inference itself
# must not download them).
#
# Scoring: pass@1, the leaderboard headline convention — one attempt per
# instance (the official mini-swe-agent baseline's budget: 6h wall per
# task, the agent-timeout default here). Trajectories + fa session logs
# ride the run dir; summary.py turns them into the registry's optional
# _stats/cost.json + _stats/calls.json (self-reported, the submission
# guide's §3 convention) and renders the accuracy/cost/calls table.
#
# gh-1503: the provider is the same dispatch surface as bench.yml /
# bench-harbor.yml — zai glm-5.3-flash (default), kimi-for-coding
# (model id == plan name; FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom` (config JSON in
# the input, key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup resolve step is
# a byte-consistent copy of bench-harbor.yml's gh-1471 step, which is
# itself a copy of bench.yml's — the cross-reference comment in all three
# files is the sync contract (gh-1685 joins it). This copy additionally
# derives the provider API host:port as outputs (the forwarder's upstream
# and the containers' /etc/hosts mapping).
#
# Quota discipline (the tbench 2.1 kimi saga, gh-1674): shards run ≤3 in
# parallel by default (max-parallel input — windowed-quota providers),
# tasks run sequentially inside a shard, a provider 429 aborts the
# remaining shard tasks immediately (exit 2, NEVER retried inline — the
# owner reruns the dispatch), and only a zero-trial startup crash gets
# the gh-1658-style single inline retry. No trial is started into a known
# dead window: the resolve step preflights the secret, and the first 429
# stops the shard instead of burning the rest.
#
# Smoke first: the default dispatch is tasks=smoke (the two
# lexicographically-first instances — a pipeline proof, NOT a leaderboard
# row: the package headline divides by the full official set, and
# summary.py's table says so). tasks=lite is the deterministic
# ~20-instance slice; tasks='' (full, ~200 instances × up to 6 LLM-hours)
# requires confirm-full-run: true.
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY     — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY    — kimi coding key (model id is the plan name)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY  — key for provider=custom → FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#
# The registry PR itself is deliberately MANUAL (docs/bench.md): download
# the programbench-submission artifact, fill in submission.yaml's
# maintainer fields (package leaves TODOs), publish the fork, open the PR.

run-name: fa bench-programbench · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks || 'full' }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'smoke (2 instances, default) | lite (~20) | comma fnmatch globs | empty = full set (needs confirm-full-run)'
        required: false
        default: 'smoke'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (same contract as bench.yml gh-1471 / bench-harbor.yml gh-1503; kimi needs FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY, custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'ONLY when provider=custom — provider config JSON {"baseUrl","model",...}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      programbench-ref:
        description: 'facebookresearch/ProgramBench ref pinning the official task set (task inventory is enumerated from this checkout)'
        required: false
        default: '895f65916bc5ba34a915d36da321fde0301125ad'
      programbench-version:
        description: 'PyPI programbench pin for eval + submit package (the submission guide requires >=1.2.0; _stats must come from one version)'
        required: false
        default: '1.2.5'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for the full (tasks-less) run — ~200 instances of LLM spend. Smoke/lite/globs are unaffected'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for the selected tasks (~4 instances/shard keeps each job inside the 6h runner window at the default agent-timeout)'
        required: false
        default: '50'
      max-parallel:
        description: 'Shards in flight (kimi saga: keep ≤3 for windowed-quota providers)'
        required: false
        default: '3'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Per-instance wall cap seconds (default 21600 = the official baseline budget; timeout kills are packed and evaluated as low scores, never silent)'
        required: false
        default: '21600'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full run holds runners for hours; queue a second dispatch instead of
# stacking them.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fa results ledger upsert (gh-1682).

`bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json` is the committed ledger of fa's OWN
Terminal-Bench results — the auto-update hook the leaderboard table
overlays on the official rows. It is written by the bench-harbor.yml
aggregate step on every completed run and by hand for backfills.

Usage (explicit fields):

    record.py --dataset-version 2.1 --model kimi-for-coding \
        --resolved 300 --total 445 --date 2026-10-18 \
        --fa-version 2fd100169e \
        --run-url https://github.com/.../actions/runs/3902812716 \
        [--run-url ...]

Usage (machine summary from summary.py --json-summary):

    record.py --summary /tmp/bench-summary.json

Idempotency contract: rows are keyed by (dataset_version, model) — one
aggregate row per dataset x model. Re-recording the same job (same
run_url) updates numbers/dates in place and unions run_urls; it never
appends a duplicate row. The 2.1 kimi row aggregates three workflow
runs (300/445 over runs 3902812716+39052822079+3909896789) exactly this
way.

Every row is self-reported evidence: `self_reported: true` is set by
this tool and the renderer leans on it for the honesty marker — never
blend fa rows into official leaderboard rows (gh-1682 AC2).

Stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

LEDGER_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name("fa_results.json")


def load_ledger(path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": 1, "results": []}
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    doc.setdefault("results", [])
    return doc


def save_ledger(doc: dict, path: Path = LEDGER_PATH) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2) + "\n")


def _key(row: dict) -> "tuple[str, str]":
    return (row.get("dataset_version", ""), row.get("model", ""))


def upsert(doc: dict, *, dataset_version: str, model: str, resolved: int,
           total: int, date: str, fa_version: str = None,
           run_urls: "list[str]" = ()) -> dict:
    """Insert or update the (dataset_version, model) row. Existing
    run_urls are unioned (sorted, deduped) so a job re-run updates
    instead of duplicating; numbers/date/fa_version reflect the latest
    record call."""
    row = None
    for existing in doc["results"]:
        if _key(existing) == (dataset_version, model):
            row = existing
            break
    if row is None:
        row = {"dataset_version": dataset_version, "model": model}
        doc["results"].append(row)
    urls = set(row.get("run_urls") or [])
    urls.update(u for u in run_urls if u)
    row.update(
        {
            "resolved": int(resolved),
            "total": int(total),
            "date": date,
            "run_urls": sorted(urls),
            # fa rows are self-reported, never official (gh-1682).
            "self_reported": True,
        }
    )
    if fa_version:
        row["fa_version"] = fa_version
    # Stable order: dataset version desc, then accuracy desc (two
    # stable passes — one tuple with reverse=True would flip both keys).
    doc["results"].sort(
        key=lambda r: -(r.get("resolved", 0) / r.get("total", 1) or 0)
    )
    doc["results"].sort(key=lambda r: r.get("dataset_version", ""), reverse=True)
    return row


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=LEDGER_PATH)
    parser.add_argument("--summary", type=Path, default=None,
                        help="JSON totals from summary.py --json-summary")
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-version", dest="dataset_version")
    parser.add_argument("--model")
    parser.add_argument("--resolved", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--total", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--date")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-version", dest="fa_version")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_urls", action="append",
                        default=[])
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.summary:
        summary = json.loads(args.summary.read_text())
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": summary.get("family"),
            "model": summary.get("model"),
            "resolved": summary.get("resolved"),
            "total": summary.get("total"),
            "date": summary.get("date"),
            "fa_version": summary.get("fa_ref"),
            "run_urls": [summary.get("run_url")] if summary.get("run_url") else [],
        }
        missing = [k for k, v in fields.items()
                   if v is None and k != "fa_version"]
        if missing:
            print(
                "::error::summary JSON is missing required field(s): "
                + ", ".join(missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
    else:
        fields = {
            "dataset_version": args.dataset_version,
            "model": args.model,
            "resolved": args.resolved,
            "total": args.total,
            "date": args.date,
            "fa_version": args.fa_version,
            "run_urls": args.run_urls,
        }
        missing = [k for k in ("dataset_version", "model", "resolved",
                               "total", "date")
                   if fields[k] is None]
        if missing:
            print(
                "error: missing required argument(s): "
                + ", ".join("--" + m.replace("_", "-") for m in missing),
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2

    doc = load_ledger(args.ledger)
    row = upsert(doc, **fields)
    save_ledger(doc, args.ledger)
    print(json.dumps(row, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import fa_usage  # noqa: E402

    """(passed, total, solved) for one instance's {branch/test: bool} map."""
    total = len(score_map)
    passed = sum(1 for v in score_map.values() if v is True)
    return passed, total, total > 0 and passed == total


def instance_usage(tdir: Path, pricing: dict) -> tuple[float | None, int | None]:

    fa session logs; (None, None) when the shard uploaded no sessions."""

    if not sessions.is_dir():
        return None, None

name: Pages

# Builds the Flutter web demo (flutter_app) into site/app and
# deploys the static landing (site/) to GitHub Pages. Pages source must be
# set to "GitHub Actions" in the repo settings.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'site/**'
      - 'blog/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'vendor/**'
      - 'office_addin/**'
      # gh-182: the ProgramBench results page renders from the committed
      # ledger — a bench-programbench aggregate push (ledger + README)
      # must redeploy fa1.dev.
      - 'bench/leaderboard/**'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - 'scripts/build_site.dart'
      - 'scripts/site_markdown.dart'
      - '.github/workflows/pages.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# One deploy at a time; queued runs must not be cancelled mid-deploy.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build landing + web demo
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily website watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # flutter web build + add-in build + a Playwright
    # chromium boot smoke; historically ~15m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # Same pinned SDK as ci.yml web-spa (#1100): fa1.dev and
          # fa-web-spa.zip must never drift onto different Flutter stables.
          # EXACT patch pin (#1431): a wildcard pin re-resolves a new
          # engine build on every 3.47.x patch drop, the canvaskit/skwasm
          # artifacts move under a new rev-hash dir and every size gate on
          # the artifact false-reds. Bump this pin consciously in the same
          # PR that reseeds any floor a real size delta moved.
          flutter-version: '3.47.7'
          channel: stable

      # gh-1275 AC3 (web leg): fail fast before the web build — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      - name: Example app pub get
        # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # the build fails without it.
      - name: Placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored too (real keys stay local). The
      # web build needs the file to compile: copy the tracked placeholder —
      # main.dart skips Firebase init for YOUR_* values, so the demo runs
      # without Analytics (as it always has).
      - name: Placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: Build web demo
        working-directory: flutter_app
        id: web_build
        run: >-
          flutter build web --release
          --base-href /app/
          --output ../build/pages/app

      # The vendored WASI interpreter assets are mobile-only (#1096 AC3):
      # assets/wasm/* loads exclusively through WasiSandboxShell
      # (env_factory_io.dart — Android/iOS); the web build compiles
      # env_factory_stub (wasm_run needs dart:ffi) and runs python/js/
      # sqlite from cdn.jsdelivr.net (web_interpreters_web.dart). ~47MB
      # of dead weight in the deploy root — prune post-build, flags
      # untouched. The extension/office panel builds prune the same set
      # inside their packaging scripts.
      - name: Prune mobile-only wasm interpreter assets (#1096 AC3)
        run: |
          # Shared prune (scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh): fails loudly on
          # flutter_assets layout drift. assets/wasm (~47MB) is loaded
          # exclusively via WasiSandboxShell (mobile-only); the pub
          # package's own test fixtures (coach_anny.glb, 5.6 MB) ride
          # along as package assets nothing on the web app loads.
          bash scripts/prune_flutter_assets.sh build/pages/app/assets \
            assets/wasm packages/js_widget_runtime/test

      # gh-1684: the Chrome extension no longer ships on the site — the
      # zip moved to GitHub Releases (releases/latest/download/
      # fa-extension.zip, what site/index.html links). It is built and
      # size-gated at PR review time (ci.yml extension-size-gate) and on
      # the release leg (build-macos.yml build-extension), so nothing
      # extension-related happens in this deploy anymore.

      # The Office add-in ships on the site too (sideload from
      # fa1.dev/outlook/manifest.xml): the script validates the manifest,
      # builds the fa web app with the office host flag (the pane IS the
      # app, outlook/app/) and assembles build/pages/root/outlook/ in
      # place — BEFORE the assemble step, so the artifact dir persists
      # into the upload.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: |
          cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && cd ../..
          bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # gh-1476 (PR #1479 owner directive): the static GEO layer is
      # generated ONLY here, straight into build/pages — the artifacts
      # (blog/docs pages, sitemap.xml, llms-full.txt) are gitignored
      # deploy-time products and never exist in the repo tree; sources
      # (blog/posts, docs/*.md, site/*.html|txt|css) are the single
      # source of truth. `--out` copies the static tree and overlays the
      # generated layer, so the Assemble step below picks up the freshly
      # built files, not repo paths. Dep-free pure Dart scripts — no
      # `dart pub get` needed.
      - name: Build the static GEO layer (gh-1476)
        run: |
          dart scripts/build_blog.dart
          dart scripts/build_site.dart --out build/pages/root

      - name: Assemble Pages artifact
        run: |
          # build/pages/root already holds the complete site: the GEO
          # step above built the generated layer AND the static tree
          # into it. Only the deploy-specific additions land here.
          mkdir -p build/pages/root
          # The App Store frames page (issue #691): the images are the
          # COMMITTED GOLDENS, copied at deploy — never hand-copied PNGs,
          # so the site assets cannot drift from the store assets (the
          # page↔golden set is pinned by test/site/appstore_assets_test.dart).
          mkdir -p build/pages/root/app-store/img
          cp flutter_app/test/goldens/store/en/ios/*.png build/pages/root/app-store/img/
          # Only copy the web app if it built successfully.
          if [ -d build/pages/app ]; then
            cp -R build/pages/app build/pages/root/app
          fi
          # gh-1684: fa-extension.zip is NOT copied into the Pages artifact
          # anymore — it downloads from the GitHub release (AC1).

      # gh-182: the ProgramBench results page — the same results block as
      # the README section, rendered from the COMMITTED ledger (updated
      # by bench-programbench.yml's aggregate; the bench/leaderboard
      # paths trigger above picks those pushes up). Hermetic: stdlib
      # renderer, no network — every run/artifact link is already an
      # absolute URL in the ledger. Deploy-time product (gh-1476): never
      # committed, generated straight into the deploy root.
      - name: Render ProgramBench results page (gh-182)
        run: |
          python3 bench/leaderboard/pbench_render.py \
            --ledger bench/leaderboard/pbench_results.json \
            --html build/pages/root/programbench.html

      - name: Cache-bust static assets
        if: steps.web_build.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          BUILD_ID: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          # Bust the Flutter demo app's entry scripts so browsers never load a
          # stale flutter_bootstrap.js / helper bundle after a new deploy.
          sed -i -E 's|src="([^\"]+)"|src="\1?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/app/index.html
          # Bust the landing page's own CSS/JS and the demo-app iframe/link.
          sed -i -E 's|href="styles\.css"|href="styles.css?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="main\.js" defer|src="main.js?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" defer|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|src="\./app/"|src="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'"|g' build/pages/root/index.html
          sed -i -E 's|href="\./app/" target="_blank"|href="./app/index.html?v='"${BUILD_ID}"'" target="_blank"|g' build/pages/root/index.html

      # gh-1684: NO size gates run at deploy time anymore. The
      # fa-extension.zip gate moved to PR review time (ci.yml
      # extension-size-gate) and the release leg (build-macos.yml
      # build-extension); the web-app/outlook-app gates were notice-only
      # since #1096 (baselines never committed — gh-1684 decision 5) and
      # are removed rather than armed: a size regression must fail the PR,
      # not the deploy.

      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5.0.0
        with:
          path: build/pages/root

      # Gate the deploy on a real-browser boot smoke: serve the assembled
      # artifact and drive headless Chromium — the app must mount and run
      # Dart main() with zero console errors. Dart tests cannot catch
      # runtime JS-interop crashes (once shipped: the extension probe threw
      # a null-check on every normal page); this can and did.
      - name: Web boot smoke (headless Chromium)
        working-directory: build/pages/root
        run: |
          python3 -m http.server 8788 --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          trap 'kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          npm init -y >/dev/null
          npm i --no-fund --no-audit playwright@1.49.1 >/dev/null
          npx playwright install chromium --with-deps >/dev/null
          node scripts/web_boot_smoke.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8788/app/

needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1682: the leaderboard step commits the updated fa-results
    # ledger + regenerated README table back to the repo.
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" \
            --json-summary leaderboard-summary.json jobs

      # gh-1682: auto-update the public leaderboard — append the run's
      # result to bench/leaderboard/fa_results.json (idempotent: keyed by
      # dataset version + model, run URLs union) and regenerate the
      # README table. Runs only on a COMPLETE full run (the verdict step
      # succeeded) — smoke/narrowed dispatches (non-empty tasks) never
      # touch the ledger.
      - name: Update leaderboard ledger & table
        if: success() && inputs.tasks == ''
        env:
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python bench/leaderboard/record.py --summary leaderboard-summary.json
          # No --version: render every ledger version + the 4.0 field,
          # so the marked README block is rewritten whole, never shrunk
          # to the dispatch's single family.
          python bench/leaderboard/render.py
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add README.md bench/leaderboard
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "leaderboard: ledger and table already up to date"
          else
            git commit -m "bench: leaderboard ledger update · ${FAMILY} · ${MODEL} (gh-1682)"
            git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
          fi

- rename the column to what it is (e.g. `Test-pass %`) and say in the section intro that it is the mean per-instance scored-test rate.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Re-running an old green run silently regresses the committed ledger**

This step records and pushes the ledger **from the run's pinned checkout**: `actions/checkout` (top of the job) pins the dispatch-time sha, so the working tree holds the ledger **as it was when the run was dispatched**. The record → render → `git push` chain then writes that whole stale tree back:

- Run A dispatched at sha S1 (ledger L0) → records L0+A → pushes.
- Run B dispatched later at S2 (ledger L0+A) → records L0+A+B → pushes.
- Someone clicks **"Re-run all jobs"** on run A months later → checkout is S1 again → the step records **L0+A**, regenerates the README section from it, and pushes — **B's row (and any hand-backfilled rows) silently disappear from the public board**, and the README section rewinds with them.

The `concurrency` group serializes *concurrent* runs but does nothing against this cross-time overwrite. The gh-1682 sibling step (`bench-harbor.yml` "Update leaderboard ledger & table") has the same shape, so this is a copied pattern — but this PR is the moment to harden it cheaply, e.g.:

```bash
git fetch origin "${GITHUB_REF#refs/heads/}"
git rebase "FETCH_HEAD"   # or: check out the branch's ledger before recording
```

before `pbench_record.py` runs (a non-fast-forward push rejection failing the step would already be better than a silent revert). Worth a follow-up for the harbor step too.

1. If `MARKER_BEGIN` exists but `MARKER_END` is missing or precedes it (a merge-conflict remnant of the generated region is the classic way), the function falls through to the anchor/heading insertion and appends a **second** generated block next to the orphaned one — the README then carries two ProgramBench sections and `--check` can never converge. Failing loudly (exit 2, "orphaned pbench-leaderboard:begin marker") would surface the corrupt README immediately.
2. `text[end + len(MARKER_END) + 1:]` assumes exactly one character (the `\n`) after the end marker; a marker at EOF without a trailing newline would silently swallow the following character into the replaced span. `text.find("\n", end)` with an EOF fallback is the robust form.

Neither bites the committed README today (the round-trip test covers the healthy shape) — this is cheap armor for the CI-only writer.
